output.brief: The August dip came from the cooling failure, not the contractor or the kiosks. Chiller CH-2, which serves floors 6-8, was down from 4 to 19 August. Rooms ran at 26.5-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Their overall score fell from 8.6 to 6.8 for stays checking out 5-20 August, then recovered to 8.4 once cooling returned. Heat made up 56 of 74 negative comments, all from floors 6-8. Floors 1-5 stayed flat overall. Cleanliness scores and inspection pass rates did not move. Kiosk use, queue times and check-in scores were also stable. The survey questionnaire and invitation method were unchanged. So I would not serve notice on Orrin, pull the kiosks, or drop the floor 6-8 responses from the score. Doing any of these would blame the wrong party or hide the problem. Next steps: restore the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers (the April budget hold is the underlying weakness), keep critical spares on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. The outage guests already received an apology and half a night's credit, so a return-stay offer is optional. The 6% rate rise may have contributed to a small value-score dip on floors 1-5, but a normal August dip hides it. Monitor it rather than reverse it. I am fairly confident in this diagnosis.
